what: G1 ablation arms: the same 4-task suite once per mechanism removed
executor: granite4.1:3b via the dedicated Ollama on 127.0.0.1:11435, CPU
deputy: off (auto_review false, approve_scoped_writes true) - these arms differ by one mechanism, and a nondeterministic LLM in the measurement path is noise the comparison cannot absorb
headline: THREE OF THE FOUR ABLATION ARMS MEASURED NOTHING. Their mechanisms never engaged on this suite, so those arms are re-runs of the control rather than comparisons with it. Only code-as-action produced a real contrast.

why_each_arm_was_inert.compaction: enforce_ceiling fires above context_fill_ratio * usable_context_window = 0.28 * 16384 = 4587 tokens. The largest single call in the whole run was 2320 input tokens (server count) and the in-loop estimator never exceeded 1916. Not once within 2x of the ceiling: 0 compaction.skipped, 0 artifact.tombstoned, 0 sessions rotated, in EVERY arm including the control.
why_each_arm_was_inert.semantic_cache: config.local.yaml sets compress_observations_over_tokens to 100000 ('effectively off') and active_local_tier to null, so _compress_observation returns before reaching cached_op. 0 compress_tool_output calls and 0 semantic_cache rows in every arm.
why_each_arm_was_inert.prefix_stability: the ablation replaces task-start snapshots with live re-reads, which only diverge if skills or tier-1 memory CHANGE mid-task. A measured arm runs skills-off and isolated, and nothing wrote memory: 0 memory.written. 4 distinct prefixes in every arm - one per task, stable across every step - so the live read returned the same bytes the snapshot would have. Its token delta against the control is exactly 0.

the_one_arm_that_measured_something.run_code_receipts: 9-10 in every other arm, 0 in this one
the_one_arm_that_measured_something.reading: the model completed the same three tasks without run_code, at more input tokens, more model calls and more wall clock. Directionally what code-as-action is claimed to buy. At n=4 it is a sighting, not a measurement.

what_this_cannot_support: G1's >=10x paid-token reduction. No paid backend was called; every cost here is 0.0 by construction on a local model.

Any effect size. n=4, one run per arm, no repeats, no variance estimate. The +2320-token 'delta' shared by the no-compaction and no-semantic-cache arms is ONE extra model call of 2320 tokens - the control took 13 calls and those two took 14 - and both arms produced byte-identical totals, which is what two runs of the same code path look like. That number is step-count variation, not a mechanism.
Anything about compaction, the semantic cache or prefix stability. Their arms did not differ from the control in any observable way.
what_it_does_support: The switches work end to end: five arms ran to completion under HARNESS_VERSION 3, each with its mechanism setting recorded in profile_provenance, and the code-as-action arm verifiably had no run_code.

The suite cannot exercise three of the four mechanisms. That is a property of bench/tasks and config.local.yaml, and it is the thing to fix before G1 is attempted again - a bigger suite is not enough on its own, the tasks have to produce observations large enough to cross a 4587-token ceiling and repeated enough to hit a cache.

CORRECTION_2026_09_22.what: every pass rate in this record is void
CORRECTION_2026_09_22.why: the task contract was rendered whole into the prompt, so output_schema's x-expected handed the model its own answer (FINDINGS 1.31). 0.75 in all five arms is the fraction of tasks carrying a grading key - three of four - and the one task without a key failed in every arm.
CORRECTION_2026_09_22.what_still_stands: the mechanism conclusions. compaction.skipped, tombstone, session-rotation, prefix-fingerprint and run_code counts are unaffected by the leak, so 'three of four arms measured nothing' holds, as do the token figures.
